title: Ajay Bhatt and the Creation of USB (1996)
explainer: In the early 1990s, Intel engineer Ajay Bhatt grew frustrated that installing a new peripheral often meant juggling IRQ conflicts, serial/parallel port quirks, and multiple reboots. He pushed for a single standardized bus that peripherals could share through one host controller, and an industry alliance formed around 1994-1995 (Compaq, DEC, IBM, Intel, Microsoft, NEC, Nortel among the founding backers) released USB 1.0 in 1996, replacing a tangle of proprietary ports with one enumerable, hot-pluggable bus. It's a concrete, well-documented case of exactly the problem this lesson's bus concepts exist to solve: how multiple devices share a limited set of wires without stepping on each other.
